In Caribbean and Latin American hotel-development discussions, the following brands are commonly evaluated for **new-build select-service, focused-service, or limited-service projects**.

### Core brands most often shortlisted

| Brand family | Common candidates | Typical positioning |
|---|---|---|
| **Marriott International** | **Courtyard by Marriott, Fairfield by Marriott, City Express by Marriott, Four Points by Sheraton, AC Hotels, Aloft** | Midscale through upscale select service |
| **Hilton** | **Hampton by Hilton, Hilton Garden Inn, Tru by Hilton** | Upper-midscale through upscale focused service |
| **IHG** | **Holiday Inn Express, avid hotels** | Midscale and upper-midscale limited service |
| **Hyatt** | **Hyatt Place**; sometimes **Hyatt House** for extended-stay demand | Upscale select service |
| **Accor** | **ibis, ibis Styles, ibis budget** | Economy through upper-economy/midscale |
| **Wyndham** | **La Quinta by Wyndham, Wyndham Garden, Ramada Encore, TRYP by Wyndham, Microtel by Wyndham** | Economy through upper-midscale |

Marriott formally classifies Courtyard, Four Points, Fairfield, AC, Aloft and several other concepts as select-service brands. **City Express by Marriott is especially relevant in Latin America**, where its efficient midscale model is designed for urban, suburban and secondary markets. ([hotel-development.marriott.com](https://www.hotel-development.marriott.com/brands/select-brands))

Hilton’s most established regional focused-service choices are **Hampton and Hilton Garden Inn**, while **Tru** has become a major pipeline brand in the region. Hilton reported more than 90 focused-service hotels in its Caribbean and Latin American pipeline entering 2026. ([stories.hilton.com](https://stories.hilton.com/releases/hilton-wraps-2024-with-record-portfolio-and-pipeline-growth-in-the-caribbean-and-latin-america))

IHG’s principal select-service flag is **Holiday Inn Express**. **avid hotels** is increasingly relevant—particularly in Mexico—although it has less regional operating history than Holiday Inn Express. ([ihgplc.com](https://www.ihgplc.com/en/news-and-media/news-releases/2025/ihg-hotels-and-resorts-strengthens-position-across-mexico-latin-america-and-the-caribbean?utm_source=openai))

Hyatt’s conventional regional candidate is **Hyatt Place**. Hyatt House is considered when the demand profile supports kitchens and longer stays; Caption by Hyatt may be evaluated for more lifestyle-oriented urban projects. Hyatt also has newer Essentials brands, but they currently have much less regional precedent. ([newsroom.hyatt.com](https://newsroom.hyatt.com/2024-10-03-Hyatt-Select-Service-Pipeline-in-the-Americas-Grows-by-More-than-25-Over-the-Past-Three-Years-Including-Over-4%2C000-Pipeline-Hyatt-Studios-Rooms))

Accor’s **ibis family** has particular strength in South America, especially Brazil and major urban markets. Novotel occasionally competes in the broader select-service set, although it is often operated more like a conventional midscale hotel with greater food-and-beverage offerings. ([group.accor.com](https://group.accor.com/-/media/Corporate/our-brands/PDF-for-pages/ibis/Why_Invest_in_ibis.pdf?rev=0b18a669b96d484eae6c4d342d6491d7&utm_source=openai))

Wyndham’s most relevant candidates are generally **La Quinta, Wyndham Garden, Ramada Encore, TRYP and Microtel**. Wyndham specifically supports new-construction prototypes for La Quinta, Wyndham Garden and Microtel, among others. ([development.wyndhamhotels.com](https://development.wyndhamhotels.com/our-brands/))

### Secondary or market-specific possibilities

Depending on country, site and developer relationship, the competitive set may also include:

- **Moxy by Marriott** — lifestyle select service in denser urban or entertainment locations.
- **SpringHill Suites, Residence Inn, Home2 Suites, Hyatt House, Staybridge Suites or Candlewood Suites** — where extended-stay demand exists.
- **Spark by Hilton** — premium economy, though frequently more conversion-oriented.
- **Four Points Flex by Sheraton** — light-operating midscale concept, but still emerging regionally.
- **Park Inn by Radisson, Cambria or Comfort** — considered selectively where Choice/Radisson distribution and franchise support are available.
- **Mercure or Novotel** — sometimes included under a broader “select-service/midscale” definition.
- **Dazzler, Esplendor or other Wyndham concepts** — particularly in South American markets.

### Practical “first-call” shortlist

For an initial feasibility or brand-selection exercise, the most typical shortlist would be:

1. **Courtyard**
2. **Fairfield**
3. **City Express**
4. **Hampton**
5. **Hilton Garden Inn**
6. **Tru**
7. **Holiday Inn Express**
8. **Hyatt Place**
9. **ibis or ibis Styles**
10. **La Quinta or Wyndham Garden**

The final set usually depends on whether the project is **Caribbean resort-adjacent, airport, urban corporate, secondary-city, roadside or extended stay**. Caribbean projects often lean toward Courtyard, Hilton Garden Inn, Hampton, Hyatt Place and AC/Aloft, while continental Latin America offers a deeper market for City Express, Fairfield, Holiday Inn Express, ibis, Tru and La Quinta.
